name: France
genZNote: France gave the world the metre, the modern human rights vocabulary via 1789, and the EU's founding push — it's basically the country most likely to show up as the answer whenever an exam asks 'where did this globally standard idea originate?'

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: The largest country in Western Europe by area, bordered by Belgium, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, Spain, and several microstates, with coastlines on the Atlantic, English Channel, and Mediterranean.
Diverse terrain including the Alps and Pyrenees mountain ranges, the fertile Paris Basin, and extensive river systems (Seine, Loire, Rhône, Garonne).
Includes overseas territories and departments (e.g., French Guiana, Réunion, Martinique) spread across multiple continents.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: French is the official language; the country has a globally influential cultural tradition in art, philosophy, cuisine, fashion, and cinema.
The 1789 French Revolution's ideals of 'Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité' (Liberty, Equality, Fraternity) remain central to French national identity.
Strong tradition of secularism ('laïcité') formally separating religion from public institutions, a distinctive feature of French governance.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A semi-presidential republic (Fifth Republic, since 1958) with a directly elected President sharing executive power with a Prime Minister, and a bicameral Parliament.
One of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council, and a recognised nuclear power.
Administratively divided into regions and departments, with a strong tradition of centralised governance from Paris.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A major global centre of scientific research, home to institutions like the Pasteur Institute (pioneering microbiology and vaccine research since Louis Pasteur's era) and CNRS.
World leader in nuclear energy generation as a share of its electricity mix, and strong in aerospace engineering (Airbus is a major Franco-European venture).
Numerous French Nobel laureates across physics, chemistry, and medicine, including foundational contributions to radioactivity research (Marie and Pierre Curie).

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A founding member of the European Union and NATO, and a permanent UN Security Council member with veto power.
Maintains significant global influence through 'La Francophonie', the international organisation of French-speaking nations and regions.
A key military and diplomatic power in Europe, Africa (given historical colonial ties), and the Indo-Pacific (through overseas territories like Réunion and French Polynesia).

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and France share a 'Strategic Partnership' dating to 1998, with defence cooperation as a major pillar, including the Rafale fighter jet deal and Scorpène submarine collaboration.
France strongly supports India's Indo-Pacific strategy and has been a key partner in India's civil nuclear energy programme (Jaitapur project) and space cooperation.
Historic ties trace back to French colonial-era Pondicherry (Puducherry), which retains French cultural influence today.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: One of the world's largest economies, strong in aerospace, automobiles, luxury goods, pharmaceuticals, and agriculture.
A world leader in nuclear power generation and a major global tourism destination, consistently among the world's most visited countries.
Major exporter of aircraft (via Airbus), wine, and high-end fashion and luxury goods.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: The 1789 French Revolution and its lasting global influence on democratic and human rights ideals.
Global leadership in fashion, cuisine, and the arts (Paris as a cultural capital).
Being one of the world's most visited tourist destinations.
A key defence and strategic partner for India (Rafale jets, submarines, nuclear cooperation).

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Euro (EUR), adopted for cash transactions in 2002.
A major global economy with strengths in aerospace, luxury goods, automobiles, and agriculture.
The world's most-visited country by international tourist arrivals.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Diverse landscapes spanning the Alps, the Pyrenees, and a long Mediterranean and Atlantic coastline.
Relies heavily on nuclear power, giving it one of the lowest carbon-intensity electricity grids among major economies.
Home to several UNESCO biosphere reserves and national parks.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Traces statehood to the medieval Frankish kingdoms and the eventual Kingdom of France.
The French Revolution of 1789 ended absolute monarchy and reshaped ideas of citizenship and republicanism worldwide.
Multiple republics have followed since, with the current Fifth Republic established in 1958.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1789 Revolution ended the absolute monarchy of the Ancien Régime.
1958 Constitution founded the Fifth Republic under President Charles de Gaulle, creating a semi-presidential system.
A founding member of the European Coal and Steel Community (1951), the direct precursor to the European Union.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: Centre National d'Études Spatiales (CNES) is a founding pillar of the European Space Agency.
The Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana serves as Europe's primary spaceport.
Strong aerospace-engineering base, home to Airbus's major operations.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Home to the Tour de France and the Cannes Film Festival, both globally significant cultural events.
Won the FIFA World Cup in 1998 and 2018.
The Louvre, Eiffel Tower, and Palace of Versailles are among the world's most-visited cultural landmarks.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: A permanent member of the UN Security Council.
Founding member of the European Union and NATO; member of the G7 and G20.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: France is a semi-presidential republic in Western Europe, a founding EU/NATO member and UN Security Council permanent member with deep global cultural and strategic influence.
keyFacts: Semi-presidential republic; current system is the Fifth Republic (since 1958).
Permanent UN Security Council member and recognised nuclear power.
Key India defence partner: Rafale jets, Scorpène submarines, Jaitapur nuclear project.
commonConfusion: France's 'semi-presidential' system means the directly elected President shares executive power with a Prime Minister — it is not a purely presidential system like the US.

highYieldFacts: France: semi-presidential Fifth Republic since 1958; permanent UNSC member.
Founding EU and NATO member; global cultural and diplomatic power via La Francophonie.
India-France: Strategic Partnership since 1998; Rafale jets, Scorpène submarines, Jaitapur nuclear project.
commonTraps: Assuming France is a purely presidential system like the US — power is shared with a Prime Minister.
Forgetting France is a recognised nuclear weapons state and permanent UNSC member.
mustRemember: France: Fifth Republic, UNSC permanent member, EU/NATO founder, top India defence and nuclear partner.
